body.estimand_functional: \(C(p)=H(\theta)/K(\theta)\) for every \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{feas}}\) with \(\mathcal F_+(p)\ne\varnothing\) and every \(\theta\in\mathcal F_+(p)\)

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite menu \(\mathcal R\) of observational and perfect-interventional regimes is supplied; symbolic identification is uniform over its full feasible image.
sampling_model.units: For inference, regime \(r\) supplies \(n_r\) i.i.d. finite-alphabet draws, independently across regimes.
sampling_model.treatment: Each regime clamps a declared endogenous subset \(Z\) to \(z\) and records the complete joint outcome on \(V\setminus Z\).
sampling_model.overlap: Evaluation distinguishes infeasible menu vectors and feasible vectors with no positive-denominator model; inference additionally imposes a fixed circuit margin and positive limiting regime fractions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No infinite-dimensional nuisance is estimated; empirical multinomial cells pass through the verified rational circuit by automatic differentiation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algorithms 1--2 and Theorems 5--6 are sound and complete for marginal and conditional counterfactual identification from arbitrary observational and experimental inputs in recursive acyclic SCMs.
Theorem 9.10 proves soundness of an extended ID algorithm for cyclic ioSCM interventional effects, and Remark 9.11 makes no completeness claim.
Theorem 2.4 gives finite canonical acyclic SCMs, and the paper reduces counterfactual bounds to polynomial optimization.
The inflation hierarchy converges asymptotically to the compatible set for finite latent causal structures.
Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 characterize source-aligned influence functions and canonical gradients for prespecified smooth data-fusion targets.

body.tldr: Finite-alphabet simple SCMs permit counterfactuals under feedback, but complete conditional counterfactual algorithms are acyclic and cyclic algorithms stop at sound interventional identification. SC-CTFID is a deterministic cycle-label- and source-incidence-preserving recursion on explicit legal response tables. It emits one rational circuit uniformly over the positive feasible menu image exactly when the conditional target is uniformly identified, and otherwise emits two verifier-accepted same-alphabet simple SCMs matching every supplied law. Its terminal retains the product of named source simplices, uses exact two-copy real elimination and function-field descent, and exposes any nonrational constant-fiber component as a diagnostic whose impossibility is the open kernel. A complete \((2,2,3)\) trace displays the 240-row legality filter and four source-induced product circuits. Returned circuits compile to multinomial influence functions and simultaneous regions, with infeasible, zero-denominator, exact, and degenerate inputs separated.

project_justification.gap: CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 proves complete conditional counterfactual identification for recursive SCMs, while BongersForrePetersMooij2021 supplies cyclic simple-SCM semantics and ForreMooij2020 proves only sound cyclic interventional identification. None gives an executable Layer-3 terminal that respects fixed-point legality and granular independent sources, states the full feasible-image quantifiers, or returns checkable same-class witnesses.
project_justification.niche: One induced chordless cycle per consolidated district permits nontrivial feedback and sparse confounding while admitting exact legality enumeration, preserved cycle labels, and finite source-polynomial elimination.
project_justification.fill: SC-CTFID combines CTFID cancellation with an ordered cyclic recursion, explicit source-aware CAD and Groebner elimination, exact certificate replay, boundary-preserving witness gluing, and automatic inference for verified rational circuits.

body.related_work: CorreaLeeBareinboim2021, Sections 3--4 and Theorems 5--6, supplies the acyclic formula-or-failure template and conditional cancellation; Theorem 6 gives exact reduction to it when the cyclic transitions are unreachable. BongersForrePetersMooij2021, Definition 8.1 and Proposition 8.2, supplies simple-SCM solvability and intervention and twin closure but not identification. ForreMooij2020, Proposition 9.8, Theorem 9.10, and Remark 9.11, informs consolidated-district extraction for cyclic ioSCMs but stops short of completeness and Layer-3 queries. ZhangTianBareinboim2022, Theorem 2.4 and Section 3, informs finite response parametrization and polynomial counterfactual objectives in acyclic graphs. NavascuesWolfe2020 proves asymptotic completeness of inflation, while WolfeSpekkensFritz2019 shows that independent sources impose polynomial restrictions beyond conditional independence; neither supplies a fixed exact rational terminal. LeeSpekkens2017 demonstrates Groebner feasibility and rational recovery in small functional structures. ShpitserPearl2008 and LeeCorreaBareinboim2020 supply acyclic countermodel constructions, and RichardsonEvansRobinsShpitser2023 supplies composable fixing kernels; the boundary lemma must additionally preserve cycle legality and primitive-source labels. LiLuedtke2023 informs the source-decomposed influence-function calculation, and Tikka2023 documents cfid as the direct acyclic symbolic consumer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The input explicitly lists response and source tables and can be exponentially larger than the graph. Exact real and comprehensive Groebner elimination justify only a doubly exponential worst-case bound. The rational-circuit theorem requires proving that the diagnostic obstruction \(O\) is unreachable; a uniformly identified algebraic but nonrational target would refute that contract without invalidating the executable diagnostic. The inference theorem is fixed-dimensional and pointwise on positive-margin strata; nonsymbolic zero-variance coordinates receive no Wald interval.
body.honest_scope: The fixed-point legality theorem, finite-source compression, latent-path realizability, worked trace, boundary gluing, global recursion, rational terminal descent, transition measure, complexity bound, and circuit inference are proof obligations. The \((2,2,3)\) enumeration, binary regression suite, rational separators, two-district transmitter, and CHSH rejection are computational evidence, not proofs. The open question is whether the exact terminal can ever return \(O\) and whether every local separator transmits. The acyclic reduction must reproduce CTFID exactly. A false failure on a product-identified trace cell, an illegal or source-merging certificate, a failed transmitter, or a nonrational uniformly identified target stops the program.
